title: Review of c43's conserved CIPS consumer (SIEXD): replicated on seed 8 with the consumer-free twin and the prey-removal fork; consumers die within 100 t of losing prey, but they are bands on prey edges that divide with their prey
summary: World copied unchanged; seed 8, 128^2, the claimed command (t=12000, --lineage-k 5). Consumer condensates form from noise as bright rods on prey droplet edges (plus a few free dots) and coexist with prey to the end (43 components): consumer persistent splits 27 (generation 2, merge/split 0.10), prey 85 (generation 8). Consumer-free twin (pred_on 0): a frozen emulsion of 78 prey with 8 persistent splits (generation 1, 78 persistent tracks). Prey-removal fork at t=3000 (tcut 3000): consumer bodies (q>0.5) 36 -> 0 by t=3100, max q 1.01 -> 0.17 at t=3100 and 0.08 (bath) by t=3600; the fed run keeps 30-40 consumers.

observations.S: rerun/seed8/sheet.png t=0: noise over the whole box
observations.X: twin_nocons/seed8 vs rerun/seed8: prey persistent splits 8 (generation 1, frozen) without consumers vs 85 (generation 8) with them; prey count 78 vs 39 at the end
observations.E: efork_t3000/seed8 frames: consumer bodies 36 -> 0 by t=3100 after the prey are removed, max q back to the bath 0.08 by t=3600; the consumer enzyme is conserved (never made from prey), so this dependence is dynamical
observations.D: rerun/seed8/FACTS.md consumer species: 27 persistent splits, generation 2 at K=5; sheet shows consumer rods splitting with the prey droplet they lie on

seeds_run.result: pass on the numbers: consumers form, divide (27, gen 2), coexist; twin frozen; prey removal kills all consumers within 100 t

controls_run.X: twin_nocons/seed8 (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration, window)

not_checked: I for the consumer as a free individual
verdicts.limitation: Weak, not Supported, because of the consumer's individuality: on my seed almost every consumer is a rod lying on a prey droplet's edge, so it reads as a cap or band of a prey-consumer composite rather than a free individual, and its 'division' is the composite pinching (the claim's strict strip test finds only 3-4 consumer divisions per seed). I is supported for prey and composites, not clearly for consumers alone. The E fork removes all prey at once; a local prey removal around one consumer would be the per-individual test. Lineage window 500 t.
